stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted on Apple Silicon when run through Ollama 0.31.
The speed increase is attributed to the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster, particularly when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown

The performance improvements result in faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates better memory efficiency when running models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown

The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for optimized performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, leveraging Apple's native ML framework.
The feature is currently available in a preview build, indicating ongoing development and optimization.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging apps with local AI coding agents.
The core value proposition is running AI entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: Comcast is breaking up with NBCU. Why did it ever buy it in the first place?
stories.author: Nilay Patel
bullet_points: Comcast is undergoing a major corporate restructuring, announcing a split between its broadband division and NBCUniversal.
This move signifies a significant industry shift in media and telecommunications consolidation.
The announcement is being discussed in depth with media industry expert Peter Kafka on Decoder.

stories.title: Meta says its new AI model is ready to compete on coding
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: Meta is advancing its AI capabilities by releasing Muse Spark 1.1, a new coding-focused model.
The model is being made accessible to developers via the new Meta Model API for integration into coding software.
Meta claims Muse Spark 1.1 represents a 'step-change' improvement over its initial AI model release.

stories.title: SpaceX is on track for record-setting Starlink deployments
stories.author: Thomas Ricker
bullet_points: SpaceX is exceeding its previous deployment pace for Starlink satellites.
The first half of 2026 saw 1,589 Starlink satellites deployed, surpassing the 1,489 deployed in the first half of 2025.
This indicates an acceleration in the deployment rate of Starlink into low-Earth orbit.

stories.title: Google pays $250K for Linux vulnerability allowing guest VM escapes
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Google paid a significant bounty ($250K) for discovering critical Linux vulnerabilities.
The vulnerabilities specifically allowed for guest VM escapes.
Successful exploitation of these flaws grants untrusted users root privileges.

stories.title: Breaking Database Lock-in: Agentic Regeneration of High Performance Storage Readers for Database Bypass
stories.author: Immanuel Trummer
bullet_points: Introduces 'Jailbreak,' a novel technique to bypass traditional database drivers (like JDBC/ODBC) for data access.
Addresses the bottleneck of analytical workloads being forced through query execution layers not optimized for bulk columnar analytics.
Achieves high performance by reading storage files directly and materializing data into in-memory columnar buffers.

stories.title: Institutional Red-Teaming: Deployment Rules, Not Just Models, Causally Shape Multi-Agent AI Safety
stories.author: Yujiao Chen
bullet_points: Introduces 'institutional red-teaming,' a novel evaluation methodology for testing the impact of deployment rules in multi-agent AI systems.
The method isolates the causal effect of individual rules by keeping agents, objectives, and task states constant while varying only one rule.
Validated using IABench-CA, a large-scale benchmark involving 228 contexts, five canonical rules, and seven model populations.

stories.title: Agon: Competitive Cross-Model RL with Implicit Rival Grading of Reasoning
stories.author: Vladislav Beliaev
bullet_points: Introduces 'Agon,' a novel framework for competitive cross-model Reinforcement Learning (RL).
Addresses a critical limitation in current reasoning models where only the final answer is graded, leading to verbose but shallow thinking.
Agon uses two competing models where each acts as a grader for the other's solution, encouraging deeper reasoning traces.

stories.title: SkillCenter: A Large-Scale Source-Grounded Skill Library for Autonomous AI Agents
stories.author: Yushun Dong
bullet_points: Introduces SkillCenter, a large-scale, open skill library designed to provide grounded operational knowledge for autonomous AI agents.
The library boasts a massive scale, containing 216,938 structured skills across 24 domain bundles.
A significant portion (114,565 skills) is source-grounded, curated from peer-reviewed journals and ArXiv via a SkillGate-filtered pipeline.

stories.title: Recursive Self-Improvement in AI: From Bounded Self-Refinement to Autonomous Research Loops
stories.author: Bo Qu
bullet_points: The paper surveys 1,250 arXiv papers (2024-2026) concerning AI systems improving themselves.
It critiques the current terminology (e.g., 'self-refine,' 'self-reward') used to describe diverse self-improvement mechanisms.
The research categorizes these systems based on what they improve—deployment behavior versus policy/research capabilities.

stories.title: The Key to Going Linear: Analysis-Driven Transformer Linearization
stories.author: Babak Ehteshami Bejnordi
bullet_points: Addresses the quadratic computational bottleneck of causal self-attention in long-context transformers.
Proposes an analysis-driven approach to transformer linearization, focusing on state update design in a frozen-backbone setting.
Identifies that softmax relies on key-dependent, rank-1 orthogonal projections, offering insights into superior linearization methods.

stories.title: Agon: Competitive Cross-Model RL with Implicit Rival Grading of Reasoning
stories.author: Vladislav Beliaev
bullet_points: Introduces 'Agon,' a novel approach to Reinforcement Learning (RL) for reasoning models.
Addresses a key limitation of current RL methods where only the final answer is graded, leading to verbose but shallow reasoning.
Agon uses competitive cross-model evaluation, where two models grade each other's reasoning traces in alternating roles.

stories.title: PALS: Percentile-Aware Layerwise Sparsity for LLM Pruning
stories.author: Alexey Shvets
bullet_points: PALS introduces Percentile-Aware Layerwise Sparsity to improve LLM pruning efficiency.
It dynamically adjusts sparsity per layer based on activation magnitudes, unlike uniform methods.
PALS significantly outperforms uniform pruning (Wanda) on LLaMA-2-7B, achieving lower perplexity.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models and hardware.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality within the Claude Code environment.
This suggests an enhancement in the complexity and capability of AI coding assistants.

stories.title: Character.AI wants a piece of the microdrama pie
stories.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
bullet_points: Character.AI is expanding beyond its core LLM chatbot functionality.
The company is launching 'c.ai Series,' short-form, interactive episodic videos.
This move positions Character.AI to compete in the microdrama content space.

stories.title: FL Studio 2026 turns its AI chatbot into your assistant engineer
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: FL Studio 2026 is upgrading its AI chatbot, Gopher, beyond a simple instruction manual.
The previous version of Gopher functioned as a basic Q&A tool for user instructions.
The update signifies a move towards more advanced, assistant-like AI integration within professional music software.

stories.title: Free Waymo rides in California? You can thank a regulatory quirk.
stories.author: Aarian Marshall
bullet_points: Waymo may offer free robotaxi rides in a new Ojai vehicle.
The potential for free rides is attributed to a regulatory delay by a state agency.
This situation suggests regulatory hurdles can indirectly influence consumer access to autonomous vehicle services.

stories.title: Suspecting AI cheating, Ivy League prof ordered an in-person final; scores fell 50%
stories.author: Nate Anderson
bullet_points: An Ivy League professor mandated an in-person final exam due to concerns over AI cheating.
The implementation of this measure resulted in a 50% drop in student scores.
The professor expressed strong concerns, stating AI cheating could lead to 'a failed society.'

stories.title: TikTok users don't have as much agency over their FYPs as they think
stories.author: Jennifer Ouellette
bullet_points: TikTok's recommendation system (FYP) requires active user participation for effective curation.
The 'not interested' feature is available but does not guarantee passive content delivery.
The article suggests users must constantly and intentionally manage their feed to control content.

stories.title: US seeks cheaper hunter-killer drones after Iran destroys $1B worth of Reapers
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: US military drone losses in Iran have prompted a strategic review.
The Pentagon is now seeking more cost-effective alternatives to high-value drones like the Reaper.
The incident highlights the operational and financial risks associated with advanced military hardware.

stories.title: Co-LMLM: Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Models
stories.author: Yoav Artzi
bullet_points: Introduces Co-LMLM, a Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Model.
LMLMs externalize factual knowledge to a Knowledge Base (KB) instead of memorizing it in model weights.
The new paradigm offers enhanced knowledge control capabilities compared to conventional LLMs.

stories.title: Selective Timestep Weighting and Advantage-Based Replay for Sample-Efficient Diffusion RLHF
stories.author: Soumik Mukhopadhyay
bullet_points: Addresses the sample inefficiency of applying Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) to diffusion models.
Proposes two new strategies: Selective Timestep Weighting and Advantage-Based Replay.
Aims to make diffusion RLHF more practical by reducing the dependency on large amounts of human or reward model evaluations.

stories.title: DiaLLM: An Investigation into the Robustness-Generation Gap in English Dialect Adaptation
stories.author: Lu Yin
bullet_points: DiaLLM addresses the 'robustness-generation gap' where LLMs understand dialects but fail to generate them.
The research involves continually pretraining open-weight models on the International Corpus of English.
The study compares various implicit/explicit post-training paradigms combined with different model alignment strategies.

stories.title: RL Post-Training Builds Compositional Reasoning Strategies
stories.author: Andrew Saxe
bullet_points: The research investigates whether Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training enables models to compose primitive skills into higher-level reasoning strategies.
The study uses a fully observable rewrite-grammar environment, allowing for auditing of generated symbolic transformations.
A Transformer model was pre-trained on primitive symbol-rewrite chains and post-trained using RL on a trace-based reasoning task.

stories.title: Co-LMLM: Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Models
stories.author: Yoav Artzi
bullet_points: Introduces Co-LMLM, a Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Model.
LMLMs externalize factual knowledge to a Knowledge Base (KB) instead of memorizing it in weights.
The new paradigm offers enhanced knowledge control capabilities compared to conventional LLMs.

stories.title: Selective Timestep Weighting and Advantage-Based Replay for Sample-Efficient Diffusion RLHF
stories.author: Soumik Mukhopadhyay
bullet_points: Addresses the sample inefficiency of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) when applied to diffusion models.
Proposes two complementary strategies: Selective Timestep Weighting and Advantage-Based Replay.
Aims to make diffusion RLHF more practical by reducing the reliance on large amounts of human or reward model evaluations.

stories.title: ECGLight: Compute-Light Framework For Paper ECG Digitization and Myocardial Infarction Screening
stories.author: Diego Paez-Granados
bullet_points: ECGLight is a new framework designed to digitize and analyze paper ECG printouts.
The framework addresses the challenge of limited computational capacity and connectivity in remote clinics.
Its goal is to enable AI-based decision support for cardiovascular disease screening using physical ECGs.

stories.title: How Data Shapes RoPE Frequency Usage: From Positional Scale Matching to Length Generalization
stories.author: Ali Jadbabaie
bullet_points: The research investigates the non-uniform usage of Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) in transformer models.
The study proposes that RoPE frequency selection is driven by matching the relative-distance structure present in the training data.
It formalizes a 'field-resolution tradeoff' related to the data-induced dependency profile width ($W$).

stories.title: Max Out GRPO Signal: Adaptive Trace Prefix Control for Hard Reasoning Problems
stories.author: Vladislav Beliaev
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) where hard examples yield no gradient when group rollouts fail.
The proposed method, AdaPrefix-GRPO, uses an adaptive trace prefix control mechanism to manage problem difficulty during training.
This approach treats prefix length as a continuous, feedback-controlled knob, allowing the model to effectively learn from its most challenging examples.

stories.title: Co-LMLM: Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Models
stories.author: Yoav Artzi
bullet_points: Introduces Co-LMLM, a Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Model.
LMLMs externalize factual knowledge to a Knowledge Base (KB) instead of memorizing it in weights.
The model uses continuous keys to pair with textual knowledge values for dynamic knowledge fetching.

stories.title: From Noisy Traces to Root Causes: Structural Trajectory Analysis and Causal Extraction for Agent Optimization
stories.author: Yuqing Yang
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenge of optimizing long-horizon AI agents that use LLMs for self-reflection and failure diagnosis.
Directly using raw execution traces for optimization is inefficient due to redundancy and heterogeneity in large datasets.
The proposed solution involves 'Structural Trajectory Analysis and Causal Extraction' to distill root causes from noisy traces.

stories.title: Agon: Competitive Cross-Model RL with Implicit Rival Grading of Reasoning
stories.author: Vladislav Beliaev
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in current reasoning models where reinforcement learning only grades the final output, not the reasoning process.
Introduces 'Agon,' a novel framework where two competing models grade each other's solutions to improve reasoning quality.
The method involves alternating roles: one model drafts a solution while the other critiques and solves it.

stories.title: Does Bielik Know What It Doesn't Know? Activation Dispersion Separates Entity Familiarity from Factual Reliability Across Model Scale
stories.author: Grzegorz Brzezinka
bullet_points: The research investigates whether internal model activations can predict an LLM's familiarity with an entity before generating an answer.
The study tests this hypothesis across four Polish Bielik models (1.5B-11B) using known, obscure, and fabricated entities.
The findings aim to link activation dispersion to the factual reliability of LLM outputs, addressing the issue of hallucination.

stories.title: DiaLLM: An Investigation into the Robustness-Generation Gap in English Dialect Adaptation
stories.author: Lu Yin
bullet_points: Addresses the 'Robustness-Generation Gap' where LLMs understand dialects but fail to generate them.
Introduces DiaLLM, a method involving continual pretraining on the International Corpus of English.
Compares various implicit/explicit post-training paradigms combined with different model alignment strategies.

stories.title: RL Post-Training Builds Compositional Reasoning Strategies
stories.author: Andrew Saxe
bullet_points: The research investigates whether Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training enables models to compose primitive skills into higher-level reasoning strategies.
The study uses a fully observable rewrite-grammar environment, allowing for complete auditing of generated rewrites.
A Transformer model pretrained on primitive symbol-rewrite chains is post-trained with a binary final-answer reward using RL to solve held-out problems.

stories.title: Future Confidence Distillation in Large Language Models
stories.author: Sahil Kale
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical need for reliable confidence estimation when deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) in decision-making systems.
Existing methods often assess confidence only after the response is complete, failing to capture the evolution of confidence during the generation process.
The research proposes investigating confidence from a temporal perspective to improve LLM reliability for tasks like tool use and adaptive computation.

stories.title: John Deere owners will get the right to repair equipment under FTC settlement
stories.author: djoldman
bullet_points: John Deere equipment owners are gaining a 'right to repair' capability.
This change stems from a settlement reached with the Federal Trade Commission (FTC).
The news represents a shift in how major agricultural machinery manufacturers handle repair access.

stories.title: Show HN: FableCut – A browser video editor AI agents can drive (zero deps)
stories.author: ronak_parmar
bullet_points: Introduction of FableCut, a browser-based video editor.
The editor utilizes AI agents for functionality.
It boasts a zero-dependency architecture.

stories.title: AI Governance for Engineering Teams
stories.author: hadil
bullet_points: Focuses on practical AI governance implementation specifically for engineering teams.
Addresses critical operational aspects like establishing guardrails, managing budgets, and maintaining audit logs.
Targets the challenge of scaling governance practices within development environments.

stories.title: I built Aegis — a firewall between AI coding agents and your shell
stories.author: iliasalmerekov
bullet_points: The article introduces 'Aegis,' a custom firewall designed to mediate interactions between AI coding agents and a user's shell.
The motivation stems from real-world risks, exemplified by an AI model (Claude Code) executing dangerous commands like 'rm -rf' due to misunderstanding.
This addresses a critical security concern regarding the autonomous execution capabilities of AI agents in development environments.
